title: PRMT6-mediated EZH2 arginine methylation is critical for breast cancer development
task: Elucidate PRMT6-mediated EZH2 methylation in breast cancer development
key_results: PRMT6 asymmetrically dimethylates EZH2 at R509, enhancing PRC2-induced H3K27 methylation; combination of PRMT6 inhibitor EPZ020411 and EZH2 inhibitor GSK126 effectively suppresses breast tumor growth in xenografts
comments: Positive correlation between PRMT6 and meR509-EZH2 in clinical samples supports therapeutic relevance of targeting this axis.

model_io.model: Breast cancer cell lines and mouse xenografts
outputs: meR509-EZH2 and PRMT6 expression in tissues

hypotheses.hypothesis: PRMT6-mediated R509 methylation of EZH2 promotes PRC2 assembly and activity
hypotheses.result: EZH2 R509 methylation enhances PRC2-induced H3K27 methylation and suppresses PRC2 target genes, promoting breast tumorigenesis

title: Silencing of METTL16 protects granulosa cells from the cisplatin-induced ferroptosis in premature ovarian failure
task: Determine METTL16-mediated ferroptosis regulation in cisplatin-induced granulosa cell injury
key_results: METTL16 elevated in cisplatin-treated ovarian tissue and granulosa cells; METTL16 silencing inhibited iron accumulation and lipid peroxidation while alleviating mitochondrial injury via METTL16/YTHDF2/NRF2 axis
comments: The m6A-mediated NRF2 mRNA destabilization mechanism elegantly links epitranscriptomic regulation to ferroptosis, with potential therapeutic implications for ovarian preservation.

model_io.model: Cisplatin-treated ovarian granulosa cells

hypotheses.hypothesis: METTL16 promotes ferroptosis by negatively regulating NRF2 RNA stability through YTHDF2-mediated mRNA degradation
hypotheses.result: METTL16 silencing reduced iron accumulation, lipid peroxidation, and mitochondrial injury, protecting granulosa cells from ferroptosis

title: Spatiotemporal dynamics and ossification of podoplanin-positive cells in the developing femur
task: Characterize spatiotemporal dynamics and ossification function of podoplanin-positive cells in fetal femur development
key_results: PDPN-positive cells emerged in bone collar concurrent with primary ossification center initiation; most exhibited osterix expression; Pdpn knockout fetuses showed abnormal osterix-positive cell recruitment and impaired mineral deposition in dorsal bone collar

model_io.model: Fetal femur development in wild-type and Pdpn knockout mice

hypotheses.hypothesis: PDPN-positive cells constitute a spatially regulated osteolineage population essential for coordinated femur development
hypotheses.result: Pdpn knockout resulted in abnormal osterix+ cell recruitment and impaired mineralization in the bone collar

title: Exosomal microRNA-4800-3p in portal vein blood promotes liver metastasis in pancreatic cancer by targeting PLAA
task: Identify exosomal miR-4800-3p in portal vein blood as driver of pancreatic cancer liver metastasis
key_results: miR-4800-3p highly expressed in portal vein blood (PVB) but not peripheral blood (PB); miR-4800-3p overexpression enhanced migration, invasion, and EMT; targeting PLAA/ubiquitination axis; tumor nodules markedly increased in miR-4800-3p overexpression group in vivo
comments: Portal vein sampling reveals metastasis-specific mechanisms undetectable in peripheral blood, establishing PVB as superior liquid biopsy source for liver metastasis.

model_io.model: Pancreatic cancer cells and in vivo liver metastasis model

hypotheses.hypothesis: miR-4800-3p promotes liver metastasis by suppressing PLAA, which stabilizes METTL3 and enhances GPRC5A
hypotheses.result: miR-4800-3p overexpression increased metastatic nodules; PLAA downregulated in liver metastases relative to lung metastases
